unresolved_must_fix.claim: The revision deleted 'Europe was waiting to see them go.' As a result, 'no one cared to hurry it' now follows the Legation's readiness to leave. 'This was all that saved his father' no longer points to Europe's complacent delay.
unresolved_must_fix.counterevidence: A general 'no one' can still be read loosely, but the causal subject is lost.

evidence.quote: Europe was waiting to see them go. So certain was the end that no one cared to hurry it.
Europe was waiting to see them go.
ready to leave England at once, and never assuming more than three months for their limit. So certain was the end that no one cared to hurry it.
So far as a private secretary could see, this was all that saved his father.

unresolved_must_fix.minimal_repair: Restore the six-word sentence 'Europe was waiting to see them go.' before 'So certain was the end'.
unresolved_must_fix.plan_relation: required (Bull Run and the three-month horizon are essential)
unresolved_must_fix.reader_effect: The reader cannot tell what saved the Minister. It may even read as if the Legation itself declined to hurry its own end.
unresolved_must_fix.title: Europe's waiting cut, leaving 'no one' and 'this' without an antecedent

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cut the sentence about quitting a safe seat in Congress with only Sumner's doubtful support. It also cut 'on whom could Seward depend? Certainly not on the Chairman.' The paragraph now jumps from the son's unfitness to 'never before... so desperate'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The revision's paragraph 4 retains 'Minister Adams had no friend in the Senate', which partly restores the logic later on.

evidence.quote: the weakest of all Mr. Adams's proofs of fitness was his consent to quit a safe seat in Congress for an exceedingly unsafe seat in London
That Mr. Adams was unfit might well be; and no one knew so well as this experienced Senator
Mr. Adams had chosen a private secretary far more unfit than his chief. In the family history, its members had taken many a dangerous risk
No doubt he could depend on Seward, but on whom could Seward depend? Certainly not on the Chairman of the Committee of Foreign Relations.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'That Mr. Adams was unfit might well be... likely to give him' sentence, or a short clause about the safe seat and Sumner's support.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (appointment section; the Minister 'leaving no friend in the Senate')
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The climactic judgment seems to rest on the secretary's unfitness rather than on the political exposure. Sumner's role as unhelpful committee chairman also fades.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'So desperate' a family risk now lacks its grounds

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cut the reason his solitude was 'doubly desperate', namely that his duties made him escort everywhere. It also cut the Russian/French rotation of troubles, so 'nothing professional in worry' and 'Empires were always tumbling' arrive without the demonstration behind them.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The V6 aphorism survives and remains intelligible in isolation.

evidence.quote: Entire solitude in the great society of London was doubly desperate because his duties as private secretary required him to know everybody
If the American Minister was in trouble to-day, the Russian Ambassador was in trouble yesterday, and the Frenchman would be in trouble to-morrow.
To him, the Legation was social ostracism, terrible beyond anything he had known. In fact he never gave his father the smallest help
No one wanted to discuss affairs. There was nothing professional in worry.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's trouble-rotation sentence before 'There was nothing professional in worry'. Also restore the 'doubly desperate... escort' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The social nightmares lose their mechanism, since he attended those functions as escort. The aphorism becomes a bare assertion instead of a punchline.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Absurd position and diplomatic-indifference aphorisms lose their premises

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision deleted 'They were glad to face the end' and the reasoning that England was waiting to strike, so they were eager to strike first. The shouts of delight are now left unexplained.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'nervous as wild beasts under the long strain' supplies a partial motive.

evidence.quote: They were glad to face the end. They saw it and cheered it! Since England was waiting only for its own moment to strike, they were eager to strike first.
Since England was waiting only for its own moment to strike, they were eager to strike first.
broke into shouts of delight. They saw it and cheered it!

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the final 'Since England was waiting...' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (the Trent news cheered by the secretaries as war; the plan prioritizes the Trent episode)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The paradox of greeting war with joy loses its logic, which follows from the Legation's belief in British hostility. The cheer reads as mere nervous release.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Trent cheer loses its stated motive

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft cut the explanation that Trent dwarfed individual effort and made zeal too hazardous. That leaves 'Surtout point de zele!' unglossed and the Trent-usefulness link implicit. The revision then also cut the reason no one remembered the satire: others were favorite targets of ridicule.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'The Trent Affair had one result personal to him' still asserts the link.

evidence.quote: Zeal was too hazardous a profession for a Minister's son to pursue, as a volunteer manipulator, among Trent Affairs and rebel cruisers.
the world had other persons--such as President Lincoln, Secretary Seward, and Commodore Wilkes--for constant and favorite objects of ridicule.
He was totally unknown; no one thought twice about the Times article. Henry Adams escaped

unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The anecdote reads as a Manchester letter mishap rather than a lesson in proportion amid Trent Affairs. The 'value of obscurity' argument is also thinner.
